subject.title: [Feature]: Add a standard AISP/AISOP proposal contract for Skill Workshop

question: Should OpenClaw standardize Skill Workshop lifecycle invariants as a core OpenClaw-native contract, an optional AISP/AISOP reference artifact, a ClawHub/bundle artifact, or no contract artifact at all?
rationale: The implementation would define authority for security-sensitive proposal lifecycle rules across docs, tests, service behavior, CLI, Gateway, and future validators, and the correct packaging is a product/security boundary choice rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Core native docs/tests contract
options.body: Add an OpenClaw-native reference contract or generated fixture under the existing Skill Workshop docs/tests path, and keep it reference/test-only unless maintainers later approve validator authority.

options.title: AISP or ClawHub reference package
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core unchanged and publish an optional AISP/AISOP or bundle-style reference artifact outside core for teams that want the contract pattern.

options.title: Decline contract artifact
options.body: Continue relying on the existing service implementation, docs, and focused tests, and close this direction as not planned if maintainers do not want another lifecycle artifact.

recommendation.title: Core native docs/tests contract
recommendation.body: Add an OpenClaw-native reference contract or generated fixture under the existing Skill Workshop docs/tests path, and keep it reference/test-only unless maintainers later approve validator authority.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest feature-history signal on the central Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle service and safety invariants.
